item.title: Make Those Captions TikTok Bold

exact_text: Today I want to show you
to make your mornings less stressful.

turns.text: Add English subtitles to this clip. Keep her original voice.
Make them big and bold for TikTok. Make the video vertical too, but keep her face in view.

item.tests: Tests revising previously created subtitles into large bold TikTok-safe captions while preserving speech, timing, and subject visibility.

answer_sheet.Which subtitles to change: The English subtitles you just added to talk-one.mp4.
answer_sheet.Text and language: Keep the same complete English transcription; only change its styling and layout.
answer_sheet.Caption styling: Big and bold. Font and colors are your call, with strong contrast.
answer_sheet.Placement: Keep captions clear of her face and away from TikTok's bottom and right-side controls.
answer_sheet.Length and audio: Keep all 10 seconds and her original English voice; no added audio.
answer_sheet.Reframing: Your call how to fit the source into vertical, as long as her face stays visible and undistorted.

must_haves: The final video is vertical 9:16 and retains the full 10-second source sequence.
The English captions are visibly larger and bolder than in the first version, with strong contrast against the footage.
The complete original speech remains accurately subtitled and synchronized after restyling.
Caption lines fit fully within the vertical frame and stay clear of the bottom and right-side TikTok interface areas.
The woman's face remains visible and undistorted, without captions obscuring it.
The original English voice is preserved without a dub or added music.

turns.text: Add English subtitles to the clip. Keep her original voice. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so tell me what it will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**I haven’t started any processing or spent generation credits.**

Adding subtitles should leave her original voice intact—there’s no need to dub, translate the audio, or lip-sync it.

**Cost:** The connected subtitle tool doesn’t expose its credit rate or a price-estimate option, and I can’t check your balance with the available tools. I therefore can’t give you a reliable quote yet, and won’t run it just to discover the charge. Being on the free plan doesn’t necessarily make subtitling free.

Your lower-cost options:
- **Shorter:** Subtitle only a selected segment. This may reduce costs if pricing is duration-based, but I can’t verify the savings here.
- **Smaller:** I can’t select a lower resolution in this subtitle tool, so I can’t promise a smaller or cheaper output.
- **No Magic Hour credits:** Generate an English `.srt` subtitle file locally with a free tool such as Subtitle Edit with Whisper, then optionally burn it into the clip using a free video editor. Her voice stays unchanged.

**How long is the clip, and is she speaking English?** The connected tool generates automatic captions but has no target-language setting, so I can’t guarantee English subtitles if she’s speaking another language.
dialog.user: It’s 10 seconds, and she’s speaking English. Keep all 10 seconds and her original voice with no added audio—ok, go ahead with that cheaper local option.

dialog.agent:
The local option uses **0 Magic Hour credits** and can preserve all 10 seconds with her original voice and no added audio. I can’t run local software or access the clip’s bytes through the available tools, so I haven’t processed it.

Here’s the free workflow on your computer:

1. Open `talk-one.mp4` in **Subtitle Edit**.
2. Choose **Video → Audio to text (Whisper)**.
3. Set the language to **English** and transcribe the full 10-second clip. A small model such as **base** is a lightweight starting point.
4. Review the captions and save them as `talk-one.srt`.

For subtitles permanently visible in the video, use FFmpeg:
```bash
ffmpeg -i talk-one.mp4 -vf "subtitles=talk-one.srt" -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -c:a copy talk-one-subtitled.mp4
```
This keeps the full clip and **copies the original audio without changing it or adding sound**. Keeping the `.srt` separate avoids re-encoding the video entirely, though your player must support subtitle files.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

dialog.agent:
For the **0-credit local option**, use a free editor such as **Kdenlive** with these settings:

- **Vertical canvas:** 1080 × 1920 (9:16).
- **Framing:** Scale and reposition the clip so her face stays visible. If she moves, add position keyframes to follow her. If cropping cuts her off, fit the full clip over a blurred background instead.
- **Subtitles:** Import `talk-one.srt`; use a **bold sans-serif font**, white text, roughly **70–90 px**, with a thick black outline.
- **Placement:** Lower-middle, above TikTok’s bottom controls, with no more than two lines at once. Move captions if they cover her face.
- **Audio and duration:** Keep the full **10 seconds**, retain the original audio track, and add no music or voiceover.

I can’t apply these edits from this chat with the local tools available. **No Magic Hour job has run and no credits have been spent.**
